root.name: French Defense: Burn Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5

overview: Black accepts the e-pawn exchange with 4...dxe4 5.Nxe4 Be7 and trades the g5 bishop for the knight, leaving a symmetrical-looking, solid French without the usual locked centre. White has a small lead in space and development but Black has few weaknesses, so play is steady and drawish. Black then plays ...c5 or ...b6 for counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Exchange on f6, then Nf3, Bd3 and castle with a slight space and development edge
Use the open e-file and the d-pawn for a small initiative

black_ideas.idea: Play ...Nbd7, ...Be7 and ...O-O; solid with the e6 pawn and the break ...c5
Trade pieces to ease the position and reach an equal ending

typical_structures.structure: White d4 against Black e6 with the e-pawn exchanged; half-open lines, no French chain

character.notes: Burn is known as a solid, lower-risk line: few weaknesses for Black, no early forcing play.

structure.notes: d5 and e4 are exchanged: d4 against e6 with a half-open e-file for White; symmetrical-ish semi-open structure.

approach.notes: A recognised main alternative for White in the Classical French.

level.notes: Plans are clear and theory is limited.

sublines_that_differ.name: Burn 4...Be7 5.e5
sublines_that_differ.how: Moves to the Classical lines (with 6...Qxe7) and a locked French pawn chain.

character.reason: Burn gives few weaknesses and steady play.

structure.reason: The French e-pawn exchange leaves a half-open file and a symmetrical centre.

approach.reason: A normal choice for strong players.

level.reason: Plans are simple but equalising requires some care.

plans.reason: Mostly piece play without a standard structural plan.
